definitions.explanation: purchasing food from a restaurant to eat elsewhere

examples.japanese: {持|も}ち{帰|かえ}りでお{願|ねが}いします。
{店内|てんない}で{食|た}べますか、{持|も}ち{帰|かえ}りですか。
examples.english: Will you eat here or take it to go?

examples.japanese: {残|のこ}った{料理|りょうり}を{持|も}ち{帰|かえ}りにした。
examples.english: I took the leftover food to go.

examples.japanese: {持|も}ち{帰|かえ}りは{税率|ぜいりつ}が{違|ちが}う。
examples.english: The tax rate is different for takeout.

examples.japanese: この{店|みせ}は{持|も}ち{帰|かえ}り{専門|せんもん}だ。

notes:
COMMON EXPRESSIONS:
- {持|も}ち{帰|かえ}りでお{願|ねが}いします (Takeout, please)
- お{持|も}ち{帰|かえ}りですか (Is it to go?)

RELATED WORDS:
- テイクアウト (takeout - loanword)
- {店内|てんない} (eating in)
- イートイン (eat-in)
- {出前|でまえ} (delivery)

CULTURAL NOTE:
In Japan, the consumption tax rate differs between eating in ({店内|てんない}) and takeout ({持|も}ち{帰|かえ}り), with takeout having a lower rate (8% vs 10%). Staff typically ask which you prefer.

KANJI READING:
Also pronounced もちかえり. {持|も}って{帰|かえ}る means 'to take home.'
